B30.capture_spec: C13: Lab render, lab-shaders/12-signal-pad.gdshader at --set activation=0.3, still 3840 x 2160, Forward+. Verified light stripe (0.345, 0.435, 0.306), dark stripe (0.282, 0.428, 0.302): a color difference of 5.7 (CIE76), the dark stripe 52 RGB from the ink color.
B30.visual_intent: Left: the ten-line pad code with line 1 then line 2 focused. Right: a real render of the pad face-on at activation 0.3 (held still; the stripes are visible there, see stripe-contrast.txt). Readout on the render when line 2 is focused: 'no lamp'.
B30.motion_claim: The focus steps from line 1 to line 2 on their names.

cues.label: fragment(): runs once for each pixel the shape covers

B32.visual_intent: Left: the pad code with line 6 (tagged with the GLOSSARY wording for fragment()) then line 7 focused. Right: the held render; a terracotta ring (grey-backed) hops across the first four stripes, one stripe per spoken number in 'zero, one, zero, one'.
B32.motion_claim: The ring hops across the first four stripes as the voice counts them.
B32.why: The stripes are already on the real render; a ring hopping across them is the 'zero, one, zero, one'.

cues.label: swizzle: picking or reordering a vector's parts: c.rgb

B33.visual_intent: Left: the pad code with line 8 focused; when the voice says 'dot r g b' the line is tagged (GLOSSARY wording: 'swizzle: picking or reordering a vector's parts: c.rgb'). Right: the held render with a ring on the first dark stripe and then on the first light stripe; readouts 'x 0.65' and 'x 1.0' land with them (multipliers in the code, not pixel ratios).
B33.motion_claim: A ring moves from a dark stripe to a light stripe, carrying x 0.65 then x 1.0.
B33.why: The two weights belong on the two stripes they weigh; the ring moving between them is the 'mix'.

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · activation swept by script

B34.capture_spec: C12: Lab-style render of lab-shaders/12-signal-pad.gdshader on quad3d, activation 0 to 1 across the whole clip (scripted sweep; the clip is as long as the beat), Forward+. Verified at activation 1: dark and light stripes read the same (0.1216, 0.7216, 0.5216).
B34.visual_intent: Left: the pad code with line 9 (`ALBEDO = mix(base, active_color.rgb, activation);`) focused. Right: a real face-on render sweeping activation 0 to 1: the rust stripes fade into flat green; a thin 0 to 1 strip under it carries a marker. A readout 'stripes gone' lands at the end.
B34.motion_claim: The stripes fade out as the marker reaches 1, and the surface ends flat green.
B34.why: Stripes that visibly dissolve are the claim; stills would need three panes and the dark one would fail the type gate.

B35.visual_intent: The pad's fragment function as a cream code box in the middle (the real lines 6 to 10, Menlo). Above it a dashed empty slot labelled 'vertex(): Godot's default', below it a dashed empty slot labelled 'light(): skipped by unshaded'. The dashes draw in, the two slots pulse once, and the fragment box gets a solid outline. All three slots share one alignment, as in the skeleton card from the first act.
B35.motion_claim: Two dashed slots draw in around the one filled function.
B35.why: The pad is the skeleton with only one slot filled; dashed empty slots make the missing functions visible.
